decisions.question: Which phase delivers NidanaModule (flutter-binding@v2 G20), which the contract's Delivery paragraph assigns to nidana.flutter.6 provisionally?

options.label: append nidana.flutter.8 after .6 and before .7
options.consequence: One more cycle (~170 lines, <=4 tasks) and one new edge, .8 -> .7, because .7 replays unrestricted; every phase stays within one PE; nidana.flutter.7 stays the last producing phase, so no consumer edge moves; the chain after nidana.runtime.14 becomes .4, .6, .8, .7 with .5 beside .6 and .8.

options.label: G20 in nidana.flutter.6
options.consequence: No new cycle or edge, but .6 grows from ~380 to ~550 lines and about nine tasks: two review sittings in one.

options.label: G20 in nidana.flutter.5
options.consequence: Same mount-binding shape as PageScope, but one G20 case constructs a ModuleScopeObserver, so .5's gate fails until .6 merges: .5 would have to wait on .6, losing the .5/.6 parallel lane, at ~540 lines.

options.label: G20 in nidana.flutter.7
options.consequence: No new cycle or edge, but ~490 lines of full-review in the composition phase, an effect-band widget reviewed together with the executor.

options.label: both module bindings in .6, widget-test bus moved to .7
options.consequence: No new cycle, but .6 ~450 and .7 ~420 lines, both above the guideline, and G17's delivery moves as well.

decisions.why: Fixture fact: the G20 case 'NidanaModules and a ModuleScopeObserver that declare one module share its scope' constructs ModuleScopeObserver and ModuleRoutes, so G20 replays only within .6's closure; that rules out .5 without a new .6 -> .5 edge. Size: the stand-in wrapper is 69 lines by wc -l (about 170 with doc comments and own tests); added to .6 or .7 it breaks the PE guideline that every other phase meets. Appending keeps every phase within one PE and keeps .7 the last producing phase, which consumers' hard edges name. Close call against folding into .7: the signal that would change my mind is review sittings on .5 and .6 showing a ~490-line full-review phase fits one sitting, which would save a cycle.

decisions.question: Which review tier does nidana.flutter.8 (the module wrapper) take?

options.label: spot-check
options.consequence: Brief proposal and short verification doc, keeping process artifacts below the ~170-line diff (the sizing floor's smell); review glances at the diff and trusts seven conformance cases.

options.label: full-review
options.consequence: Matches .5 and .6, the other scope bindings, but the full artifact set would likely exceed the diff of a ~170-line phase.

decisions.why: The wrapper composes BusProvider.of, bus.module and one reference; G20's seven cases pin mount, unmount, failure, rebind and shared scope; the Flutter lifecycle facts it rests on are measured in the contract's experiment (N1 to N6). A spot-check is 'well-constrained with clear contracts'. The signal that would change it: lifecycle defects found in .5 or .6 that their fixtures missed.

decisions.question: Where is the placement of NidanaModule recorded: folded into D1 (the phase cut) or as a new plan decision?

options.label: new D12, D1 restated to point to it
options.consequence: The placement, its fixture fact, sizes and four alternatives sit in one decision; D1 stays a short statement of the bands.

options.label: fold into D1
options.consequence: One decision for the cut, but D1 grows by a page of alternatives specific to one widget.

decisions.chosen: new D12, D1 restated to point to it
decisions.why: The placement is a choice this re-plan took, with its own alternatives and signal; a new id keeps D1's first text and its restatement legible. No evidence beyond readability.

decisions.question: D7: how does a topic widget treat its subscription's first values now that bus-api@v2 G17 and G34 connect a subscription made during bootstrap at start(), and does the widened reference still hold under bus-api@v2 G41 and G18?

options.label: widened reference; skip first values only when bus.lifecycle is not bootstrapping at listen
options.consequence: Meets flutter-binding@v2 G5 and G6: no double frame after start(), and the frame after start() renders what a topology's connection settled; a widget mounted from work start() runs counts as after start(), as bus-api@v2 G34 says.

options.label: skip first values in every case (D7 as first written)
options.consequence: Fails the new G5 bootstrap case: the initial value stays on screen when a connection set the topic and no later publish came.

options.label: skip none in any case
options.consequence: Every mount after start() renders its first frame twice; nine G5 and G6 cases fail.

options.label: typed subscription at T
options.consequence: Under bus-api@v2 G41 an off-type value arrives as a TypeError error event, which G5's error rule turns into a widget that never rebuilds again, or, without onError, an error in the listen zone.

decisions.chosen: widened reference; skip first values only when bus.lifecycle is not bootstrapping at listen
decisions.why: The S63 adapter v2 does exactly this and passes all 69 adapter cases on the bus-api@v2 stand-in runtime; its seeded defects show the other two skip rules failing G5/G6 cases. bus-api@v2 G41 strengthens the widened reference: a typed subscription would now end the rebuilds. flutter-binding@v2 G5 and G6 already state both rules, so no amend is emitted.

decisions.question: Which plan-written decisions are restated and which only checked?

options.label: Restated: D1, D2, D3, D6, D7; Checked: D4, D5, D8, D9, D10, D11
options.consequence: Restated where what the plan does changed (eight phases, the declaration list, a new file, the chain and its closure, the first-value rule); Checked where the decision stands and only its citations or its description of contract text moved, the first text quoted in the dated paragraph.

options.label: Restated for every decision whose body text changed
options.consequence: D8, D10 and D11 would read as changed decisions although their rules are unchanged and already folded into flutter-binding@v2 (v1 amendments (b) to (d)).

decisions.chosen: Restated: D1, D2, D3, D6, D7; Checked: D4, D5, D8, D9, D10, D11
decisions.why: The house convention: a restated decision quotes its first text in a dated 'Restated 2026-10-21' paragraph, a decision checked and found still true gets a dated 'Checked 2026-10-21' paragraph. D8, D10 and D11 described v1's pre-amendment wording in the present tense; their bodies now state the rule and cite flutter-binding@v2, and the Checked paragraph quotes what the first text said, so no live line cites a superseded version.

decisions.question: Does nidana.flutter.4 (and through it .5 to .8) need a new edge to nidana.runtime.15, which lands start()'s step 2 (bootstrap subscriptions), for the G5 and G6 bootstrap cases?

options.label: keep the edge on nidana.runtime.14
options.consequence: bus-api@v2's Delivery keeps nidana.runtime.14 as the last producing phase and the phase every hard edge of nidana.flutter.4 to .7 waits on; nidana.runtime.15 runs between nidana.runtime.7 and .8, inside that closure; G42 is delivered by nidana.runtime.14 itself. Dependencies lines now name G34 and G42.

options.label: add an explicit edge to nidana.runtime.15
options.consequence: Redundant with the closure, and the record's rule keeps existing edges unless the change requires another.

decisions.why: Producer phase ids come from the contracts' Delivery paragraphs: bus-api@v2 Delivery says step 3 at nidana.runtime.7, step 2 at .15, step 1 at .12, G34 replaying from .12 on, G42 at .14, and .14 replays both bindings unrestricted, so its closure holds every producing phase.

decisions.question: nidana.flutter.2 and .3 change only in the contract versions they cite (topology-dsl@v2, flutter-binding@v2 Refinements 1 and 2). Do their Scopes name the intake record?

options.label: no: citation moves only
options.consequence: hsdd-checkpoint lists only phases with work for the request under the record's Produced; .2 and .3 keep their scope, gate and dependencies.

options.label: yes
options.consequence: The checkpoint would count two phases as work of the request that do nothing for it.

decisions.why: DEC-910's reading for nidana.runtime: a phase names the record when its scope, gate, dependencies or verification changed for v0.15.1, plus appended phases. .2's holder counts still serve G8 under v2 (every mount activates; the release's 'became unheld' decides deactivation); .3's router is unchanged by v2 Refinement 2. A bullet under the summary table records which phases were rewritten and which only moved citations.

decisions.question: PageScope under bus-api@v2 G23 and flutter-binding@v2 Refinement 4: does nidana.flutter.2's holder-count algebra change now that every mount activates?

options.label: leave .2 unchanged; .5 activates at every mount and uses the release result to deactivate
options.consequence: The pure counts still answer 'became unheld' on release; their 'was unheld' on acquire is no longer needed to decide activation but stays harmless. No rewrite of .2.

options.label: rewrite .2's counts to release-only
options.consequence: A rewrite of a pure phase for a bit the effect phase stops reading; .2 would then name the record.

decisions.chosen: leave .2 unchanged; .5 activates at every mount and uses the release result to deactivate
decisions.why: Refinement 4 changes the effect (activate on every mount, rethrow TopologyConflict, leave earlier mounts' activation), not the count algebra. No evidence needed beyond the contract text.

decisions.question: nidana.flutter.8 binds in the wrapper's first didChangeDependencies (before its child builds) and releases in dispose (after its subtree's States are disposed). Is that ordering a semantic consumers rely on that needs an amend of flutter-binding@v2 G20?

options.label: no amend: the contract already pins it
options.consequence: Terms define mount and unmount as the State's insertion and disposal, which Flutter orders parent before child and child before parent; G20's 'fails to mount ... builds no child' case pins acquire before the child builds; G4 relies on the same disposal order.

options.label: amend G20 to state the order explicitly
options.consequence: A clearer guarantee for pages under a wrapper that read module topics, at the cost of a contract change and probably a new case.

decisions.chosen: no amend: the contract already pins it
decisions.why: The Terms plus the G20 failure case leave no other conforming implementation; the stand-in does exactly this and passes. The signal that would change it: a consumer plan (nidana.integration's module slice) that needs the order stated, or a review that reads 'at mount' as allowing a post-frame acquire.
